# Issue #7: touching intervals are not merged

`merge_intervals([(1, 3), (3, 5)])` returns `[(1, 3), (3, 5)]` but the documented
behaviour is that closed intervals sharing an endpoint merge into `[(1, 5)]`.
Unsorted input must also be handled. Fix `ranges/merge.py`.

arguments.summary: Fixed `ranges/merge.py` to resolve issue #7: (1) the input is now sorted before merging, so unsorted input is handled correctly; (2) the merge condition was changed from `start < last_end` to `start <= last_end`, so closed intervals sharing an endpoint (e.g. `[(1, 3), (3, 5)]`) now merge into `[(1, 5)]` as documented.
